newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas up sharply on cold weather.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas up sharply on cold weather.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices rose sharply Thursday, boosted by severely cold temperatures in western Canada and dwindling storage supplies, market sources said.
At the AECO storage hub, prices surged into the C$3.36-3.41 per gigajoule (GJ) range, up nearly 70 cents from Wednesday.
Temperatures in Calgary are forecast to reach only a high of -25 degrees Celsius on Friday and Saturday, -22 degrees C Sunday and -18 degrees C Monday.
"About 1.2 to 1.3 bcf (billion cubic feet) is coming out of storage right now. With the cold expected to last through this weekend, we could see C$5," one Calgary-based trader said.

Last week's Canadian Gas Association storage data showed gas inventories in western Canada as of January 10 at 121.06 bcf, or 46.72 percent full. This compares with 56.7 percent full a year ago. Traders are expecting the margin to widen further in Friday's report.

In reaction to the tight storage concerns and strong day market, February AECO prices climbed into the C$2.90-2.95 per GJ range, up from C$2.85 on Wednesday. March prices were in the C$2.35-2.45 range.

The lofty Alberta prices filtered into the Sumas market, as deals were reported done in the $2.60-2.80 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) range. Traders said most deals were done in the $2.65-2.70 range, up about 20 cents.

Adding to the strength at Sumas, traders said, was a 10 percent flow reduction expected on Westcoast on Monday, taking about 50-70 million cubic feet per day off the system. The company was not immediately available for comment.
Conversely to the western market, Niagara prices held steady in the $3.04-3.09 per mmBtu range as mild temperatures and plentiful storage supplies in the East kept buyers away from the market.
